adjustedProfit.title: Statutory vs adjusted operating profit & earnings
adjustedProfit.content:
Statutory operating income and net income are the GAAP/IFRS figures from the income statement. Adjusted operating profit and adjusted earnings are Centrica's own non-GAAP measures, stripping out exceptional items and mark-to-market movements on commodity trading and hedging contracts.

For Centrica plc: the statutory line is not a reliable read on the business -- operating margin swung from 24.6% in FY2023 to 0.5% in FY2025 purely from one-off items and commodity-contract revaluations, not from the underlying energy supply and generation business changing that much. Statutory EBITDA is not even populated here because it isn't meaningful. Management and analysts size the dividend and capex programme off the adjusted numbers.

What to watch:

  • The gap between statutory and adjusted lines -- a wide, volatile gap means commodity hedging/trading noise, not operating performance, is driving the statutory figure
  • Trend in adjusted operating profit and earnings across years, since the statutory trend is not informative on its own

adjustedNetCash.title: Adjusted net cash / (debt)
adjustedNetCash.content:
Centrica's own net debt/cash measure: cash and cash-like balances less borrowings and other adjustments management includes (e.g. related to decommissioning and hedging collateral), reported at FY only.

For Centrica plc: the group moved from adjusted net debt to a net cash position after FY2021 and has used that headroom to fund growth capex (Sizewell C nuclear, Grain LNG, Severn CCGT) while pausing share buybacks. The trend in this figure is the direct read on whether that capex programme is being funded from the balance sheet or will need external financing.

What to watch:

  • Adjusted net cash shrinking as capex ramps on Sizewell C and the gas-fired/LNG projects
  • Whether buybacks resume once the capex programme is more advanced

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Centrica plc: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Centrica plc: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Centrica plc: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Centrica plc: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Centrica plc: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Centrica plc: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Centrica plc: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Centrica plc: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Centrica plc: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
